surfaces.part: top header frame with white sign plate

answer.evidence: The sign is a face-on vertical board. Rows 1-2 at the top (a lighter #b27361 row, then #8b4f3f) are only a 1-2 row rim. They have no front-edge line and no eave shadow, and the width goes 12→14→16 as a frame outline would. Rows 3-5 are a white sign plate drawn face-on, which is a vertical panel. Rows 9-28 are the board face with white lettering. Rows 29-31 are a dark grey base strip. No ellipse, roof or contents are visible, so there is no real top surface. It reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical standing sign with a brown body and a cream face carrying the 카페 lettering. It has 8 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown, matching the references. Shading looks shallow, at about 4 steps on the body (a lit edge, mid, dark, outline) against about 5-6 on kiosk-a and vending-a. It has little grain or per-surface texture beyond the lettering. On a thin, simple prop this is acceptable and is not a sticker look. It is still somewhat flatter than the richer references (vending-a, kiosk-a), so I fail it by the strict 'when in doubt, fail' rule.
